High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Appellant - Manoj Kumar Bansal has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(f), 376(2)(n), 376(3) of the IPC and Section 5(j)(ii)/6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years with fine of Rs.2,000/-, rigorous imprisonment for 20 years with fine of Rs.2,000/-, rigorous imprisonment for 20 years with fine of Rs.2,000/- and rigorous imprisonment for 20 years with fine of Rs.2,000/- respectively with default stipulations, as mentioned in the impugned judgment.
The case of the prosecution is that on 07.10.2018 the accused entered the house of the prosecutrix and committed sexual intercourse with her.
It was informed to her parents.
Thereafter, a complaint was lodged against the accused.
On investigation, a charge-sheet was filed.
On trial, the appellant was convicted and sentenced as mentioned hereinabove.
Learned counsel for the appellant contends that there is no material to implicate the accused.
There is a delay of five months in lodging the complaint.
That, even according to the case of the prosecution sexual intercourse took place for almost 15 days.
Therefore, the same is with consent.
Hence, he pleads that the appellant be enlarged on bail.
The same is opposed to by the learned Public Prosecutor for the State.
On hearing learned counsels, we do not find any ground to enlarge the appellant on bail.

So far as the question of delay in lodging the FIR is concerned, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a catena of judgments have held that whenever the offence is relatable to Section 376 of the IPC, the question of delay becomes secondary especially in view of the background and the manner in which the offences have been conducted.

So far as the prosecutrix and the appellant's committing the Manoj Kumar Bansal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27503453/
1 offence for a period of 15 days is concerned, the same would not be of any avail in the case of appellant, since admittedly the prosecutrix was a minor.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The consent of the minor is inconsequential.
During investigation, it was also found that the prosecutrix was pregnant for 16 weeks.
The DNA report also supports the case of the prosecution that the act has been committed by the appellant.
Hence, we do not find any ground for the appellant to be enlarged on bail.
Consequentially, I.A.No.13374 of 2022 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail is dismissed.

(RAVI MALIMATH) (VISH  CHIEF JUSTICE   PG Manoj Kumar Bansal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27503453/
